'''Mark L. Winston''' is a [[Canadians|Canadian]] biologist and writer.<ref name=unassuming>[https://theprovince.com/technology/unassuming+scientists+have+changed+world/11170953/story.html "B.C.’s unassuming scientists have changed the world"]. ''[[The Province]]'', June 28, 2015.</ref> A professor of apiculture and social insects at [[Simon Fraser University]], he spent much of his career studying [[bees]]<ref name=unassuming/> until becoming founding director of the university's Centre for Dialogue in 2006.<ref name=director>[https://www.sfu.ca/dialogue/about-us/fellows/mark-l--winston.html "Mark L Winston"]. ''Centre for Dialog'', March 19, 2017.</ref>

His 2014 book ''Bee Time: Lessons from the Hive'' won the [[Governor General's Award for English-language non-fiction]]<ref name=announce>[https://montrealgazette.com/entertainment/arts/robyn-sarah-guy-vanderhaeghe-among-recipients-of-2015-governor-generals-literary-awards "Robyn Sarah, Guy Vanderhaeghe among recipients of 2015 Governor General's Literary Awards"]. ''[[Montreal Gazette]]'', October 28, 2015.</ref> and was shortlisted for the Science in Society General Book Award.<ref>[http://www.cbc.ca/books/2015/04/bob-mcdonald-finalist-for-science-in-society-general-book-award.html "Bob McDonald finalist for Science in Society General Book Award"]. [[CBC Books]], April 14, 2015.</ref>

==Works==
*''The Biology of the Honey Bee'' (Harvard University Press, 1984)
*''Killer Bees: The Africanized Honey Bee in the Americas'' (Harvard University Press, 1992)
*''Nature Wars: People vs. Pests'' (Harvard University Press, 1997)
*''Travels in the Genetically Modified Zone'' (Harvard University Press, 2002)
*''Bee Time: Lessons from the Hive'' (Harvard University Press, 2014)
